input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

high-severity platform outages:

1. Declare a severity-1 incident on PagerDuty notifying the primary on-call site reliability engineer within 60 seconds.
2. Initiate an emergency incident triage video conference bridge and designate an incident commander to lead operational coordination.
3. Record all incident timeline events and communications in incident channel incident-outage.md in real time.
4. Inspect external network monitoring dashboards on ThousandEyes verifying global ingress availability across 70 vantage points.
5. Examine edge load balancer error distributions identifying affected geographic regions and origin backend server clusters.
6. Inspect application container pod status in Kubernetes identifying crashing containers and pod restart loops.
7. Check database connection pool metrics on Datadog verifying available connections and transaction rollback ratios.
8. Review recent production deployment change logs identifying code releases or infrastructure changes deployed within the last 2 hours.
9. Execute automated rollback scripts rollback_deploy.sh to restore the previous known-stable container image if a code regression is identified.
10. Scale up replica counts for front-end API gateway deployments to absorb unexpected traffic surges.
11. Flush corrupted transient cache keys in Redis clusters using surgical key invalidation commands.
12. Verify that downstream asynchronous payment queues in RabbitMQ continue processing transactions without dead-letter message accumulations.
13. Publish external system status updates on our public status page every 15 minutes informing impacted customers of remediation progress.
14. Verify that incoming API error rates drop below 0.01% across all availability zones.
15. Confirm that database p99 query latencies return to baseline levels below 10 milliseconds.
16. Conduct a formal incident debriefing meeting within 24 hours documenting root cause analysis and preventative action items.

The director of platform engineering mandates that all remediation actions executed during the incident require dual-engineer verification. The security operations lead requires collecting forensic memory dumps from affected server nodes before terminating suspect instances. Site reliability engineers must ensure that automated post-mortem tickets in Jira link directly to incident logs and Prometheus snapshot metrics.
17. Verify that secondary database replicas are receiving write-ahead log streams without replication delay.
18. Inspect Kubernetes node condition events identifying disk pressure or memory pressure on worker nodes.
19. Check Elasticsearch ingestion pipelines ensuring log indexing throughput keeps pace with incoming event streams.
20. Validate that customer authentication tokens generated before the outage remain valid after service restoration.
21. Inspect S3 storage bucket permissions verifying that object uploads execute with server-side encryption.
22. Check Redis cache hit ratios confirming that application caches have repopulated critical session keys.
23. Verify that internal service discovery records in Consul reflect active container IP addresses.
24. Inspect API rate limiting metrics ensuring traffic shapers do not throttle legitimate customer requests.
25. Check firewall connection tracking tables verifying state tables are within 30% capacity.
26. Validate that automated database backup snapshots complete successfully without lock contention.
27. Inspect message processing latency in Apache Kafka ensuring consumer groups process partitions without backlog.
28. Check external monitoring Pingdom probes confirming 100% global uptime across all endpoints.
29. Verify that security operations monitoring in Wazuh detects zero unauthorized lateral movements.
30. Check SSL certificate validity across all public domain names verifying expiration is beyond 30 days.
31. Execute automated performance benchmarks confirming end-to-end transaction latency meets service level agreements.
32. Record all post-incident remediation tasks in Jira with assigned engineering owners and due dates.
33. Verify that network socket buffers in Nginx handle high connection concurrency without dropping packets.
34. Inspect database read replica lag metrics ensuring replication delay remains below 5 milliseconds.
35. Check that automated snapshot scripts complete backups across all cloud storage buckets without errors.
36. Validate that customer notification webhooks are retried with exponential backoff on transient network failures.
37. Verify that distributed Redis clusters maintain memory usage below 60% of allocated capacity.
38. Inspect host network interfaces on server instances verifying zero dropped packet counters.
39. Check that log shipping agents in Fluentbit resume streaming event logs without memory backpressure.
40. Verify that system health check endpoints return HTTP 200 with detailed component health statuses.
41. Confirm that load balancer health check thresholds require 3 consecutive successes before re-enabling instances.
42. Conduct a formal post-mortem retrospective and publish the incident report to `engineering_wiki.internal`.
43. Verify that API client connection counts return to standard operating levels on all edge load balancers.
44. Confirm that automated error alert thresholds in PagerDuty are reset to standard production sensitivities.
45. Conduct a final stakeholder briefing summarizing incident resolution timeline and business impacts."}]
